title: Nala forgives
hook: a trap made of love brings Nala home, and when Kali finally leaves him, Nala lowers the hand raised to curse

segments.voice: Yesterday: Karkotaka, whose bite began to drive Kali out, and the verse of four names. Your line was reciting Nala's story is a prayer against Kali.

The answer comes back to Vidarbha. A charioteer in Ayodhya heard Damayanti's question and answered it with a defense of a husband who had lost even his cloth to the birds. Nobody but Nala would know that. So Damayanti sets a trap made of love. She sends word to King Rituparna: Damayanti is choosing a husband again, and the ceremony is tomorrow. Only Nala could get a king there in time, so if Rituparna arrives, she'll know who drove him.
screen: `THE ANSWER COMES BACK.` → `A SWAYAMVARA, TOMORROW.` → `A TRAP MADE OF LOVE.`

segments.voice: Rituparna calls Vahuka, and Nala's heart sinks. Would she really marry again? But he drives, so fast the king's upper cloth blows away. On the road, Rituparna shows off: he glances at a Vibhitaka tree and names exactly how many leaves and fruits it holds. Vahuka cuts it down, counts, and the king is right. So they trade, the secret of dice for the secret of horses. The moment Nala knows the dice, Kali comes out of him, spitting out the serpent's poison. Nala, furious, is ready to curse him. And Kali, trembling, begs: spare me, and those who tell your story will be free of fear from me. Nala lets him go, and Kali slips into the Vibhitaka tree. At Vidarbha there's no ceremony at all. Damayanti knows the thunder of that chariot. She sends their children to the charioteer, and he weeps. The swayamvara, she tells him, was only ever a way to find him. Nala puts on the serpent's garment and is himself again. Later he wins his kingdom back at dice from his brother Pushkara, and then forgives him and sends him home in peace. Now the teaching. Kshama, forgiveness, is one of the great virtues of Hindu dharma. Earlier in the exile, Yudhishthira told Draupadi that forgiveness is truth, forgiveness is sacrifice, and the world is held together by it. Nala lives it twice: he spares the spirit that wrecked his life, and the brother who took his throne. And that promise, made because Nala forgave, stands behind the verse of four names. For today: forgiveness isn't pretending it didn't happen. It's the power to strike back, unused.
screen: `THE RIDE TO VIDARBHA.` · `KALI LEAVES NALA.` · `REUNITED AT VIDARBHA.` · `PUSHKARA SENT HOME IN PEACE.` · then, large: `KSHAMA: FORGIVENESS IS A STRENGTH.`

segments.voice: Many Hindus end their puja with a short prayer asking forgiveness for any mistakes made in it. Bring to mind someone you've been holding something against. You don't have to forgive them yet; just notice the curse you've been holding ready, and loosen your grip on it a little with each breath out. If you pray, ask forgiveness for your own mistakes and strength to give it; if not, simply rest with that open hand.
Vibhitaka. The tree where Kali hides, once Nala lowers his hand and lets him go.
Your line: kshama: forgiveness is a strength. Nala had the curse ready, and didn't use it. Until tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 794 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: SAVITRI, BORN OF A PRAYER.`
